scope: All GloBI records matched by sourceTaxon=Cirsium or targetTaxon=Cirsium, 1,000-row pages until both endpoints exhausted

query_coverage.source_field_note: The collector's source_namespace/study_source_citation/study_doi fields are all empty in returned CSV. study_title retains integrated citation text; this field must be used for provenance; no independent-study claim from record counts.

observation_quality.warning: Record keys and mirrored relations do not guarantee independent field observations. No direct head-specific location or reproductive fitness measurements in the normalized exports.

Cirsium pendulum.scope: Retrieved edges are host/fungal pathogen association only; cannot infer pollinator absence

japan38_authority_subset_gate.note: Presence is just one source claim and missing means unrecorded under this API; not population-by-trait measures.

parasitoid_second_hop.source_run_retained: No parasitoid incidence, stage, seed fitness, or trait-mediated accessibility is identified by an insect–parasitoid edge alone.

literature_positive_control.evidence: Measured ovipositor lengths plus position of larvae demonstrate parts of capitulum as parasitoid-free refuge
literature_positive_control.GloBI_role_gap: Full plant-centric query has C. heterophyllum interactsWith Pteromalus caudiger but completed T. conura-specific parasitoidOf/hasParasitoid second-hop does not recover P. caudiger. Generic plant–wasp edge does not establish direct parasitoid–host edge.

immediate_biological_question: Does developmental head reorientation and involucral access change the relative access of seed-feeding insects and their parasitoids BEFORE irreversible seed damage, and does that predict viable achene output across independent Cirsium populations?
